description: Works out a car budget from the monthly payment someone is comfortable with: the most that can be financed, the highest out-the-door price after the trade-in tax credit, that ceiling as dealers quote it (before the credit), and the vehicle price it leaves after the state's tax and typical fees. With a fair price from research, it also gives an opening offer and a walk line. Use it before shopping, when the starting point is a payment rather than a price. Numbers only; nothing is stored.

apr.description: Loan APR in percent (6.49 means 6.49%); a pre-approval rate if they have one

city.description: City or county in the state's rate table (23 states; state_rules says which), like Pittsburgh or Allegheny County: sets the combined rate from the state's own rate file. Where a city is in several counties (Chicago, Milwaukee), give county too. A place name only, never an address or ZIP

condition.description: New or used: a state's tax can differ by condition

county.description: County from the state's list (Pennsylvania, Nevada, Wisconsin; state_rules lists them), like Allegheny County: sets the combined rate. A county name only, never an address or ZIP

doc_fee.description: Expected doc fee; leave out to assume the state's cap, or a typical $450 where there is none

fair_price.description: A fair vehicle price from research, before tax and fees

invoice.description: Dealer invoice, for a new car, if known

max_payment.description: The highest monthly payment the person is comfortable with

state.description: Two-letter state code (DC included), like PA

tax_rate.description: Combined sales tax rate as a decimal (0.08 for 8%); leave out to use the state's rate

trade_offer.description: Best written trade-in offer, if any

trade_payoff.description: What is still owed on the trade-in

name: what_can_i_afford
title: What can I afford
